counting_note: Punjabi has no classifiers — put the number straight before the noun. But the noun itself goes plural: ਇੱਕ ਕਿਤਾਬ (one book), ਦੋ ਕਿਤਾਬਾਂ (two books), ਤਿੰਨ ਰੁਪਏ (three rupees).

culture.en: The Golden Temple in Amritsar: Sikhism's holiest shrine, open to everyone, day and night.
The free community kitchen at every gurdwara — sit on the floor, eat dal-roti, all are equal.
The spring harvest festival (13 April) — and the Khalsa's birthday. Expect bhangra.
The mid-January bonfire festival — peanuts, rewri and folk songs around the fire.
Punjab's thundering harvest dance — now a global party soundtrack. Women answer with ਗਿੱਧਾ (giddhā).

negation_note: ਨਹੀਂ (nahīn) goes before the verb: ਮੈਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਖਾਂਦਾ (I don't eat), ਉਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਇਆ (he didn't come). For commands use ਨਾ or ਮਤ: ਇੱਥੇ ਨਾ ਬੈਠੋ (don't sit here).

present_note: The present is stem + -ਦਾ (m) / -ਦੀ (f) + helper: ਹਾਂ (I), ਹੈਂ (tūn), ਹੈ (is), ਹੋ (tusīn — always plural!), ਹਨ (they). So ਮੈਂ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I eat, m), ਤੁਸੀਂ ਖਾਂਦੇ ਹੋ (you eat, respectful), ਉਹ ਖਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ (they eat).

ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਨਾਮ ਕੀ ਹੈ? = what's your name — answer ਮੇਰਾ ਨਾਮ … ਹੈ (my name is …).

quiz.q: The past tense 'ate' (said by a man) is…

quiz.explain: Punjabi past tenses are ergative: the verb agrees with the object — ਰੋਟੀ is feminine, so ਖਾਧੀ.
ਚੰਗਾ ਫਿਰ (changā phir) — literally 'right then!' — is the casual goodbye.
ਜੀ ਆਇਆਂ ਨੂੰ (jī āiān nū) — 'to your honoured arrival' — the warm Punjabi welcome.
ਕਿਤਾਬ (kitāb) = book — ਕਲਮ = pen, ਚਿੱਠੀ = letter.
ਦੋਸਤ (dost) = friend — ਦੁਸ਼ਮਣ is the opposite!
ਇਹ ਕਿੰਨੇ ਦਾ ਹੈ? = how much is this — then counter with ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ ਸਸਤਾ ਕਰੋ!

quiz.explain: ਕੱਲ੍ਹ (kallh) covers both — tense and context tell you which. ਪਰਸੋਂ = the day beyond.

script_note: Gurmukhi has 35 core letters — the ਪੈਂਟੀ ਅਖਰ (paintī akhar, 'the 35'). It runs left to right with no headline bar, and its letters look rounder than Devanagari. Six dotted letters (ਸ਼ ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼ ਲ਼) cover Persian sounds, and nasalization is marked with ਬਿੰਦੀ (ਂ) and ਟਿੱਪੀ (ੰ): ਮਾਂ (mān, mother) needs its bindi — drop it and the word breaks. Across the border, Pakistani Punjabi is written in Shahmukhi (Perso-Arabic) — same language, different script. Punjabi is tonal: ਘ ਝ ਢ ਧ ਭ and ਹ colour the pitch of nearby vowels — listen more than you read at first.
